title: ScaleDown Launches AI Models 467x Cheaper Than Frontier LLM APIs
summary:
A new architecture of task-specific AI models from ScaleDown eliminates the traditional generative loop to handle routine data processing at a fraction of current expenses. The company released a family of Constrained Decoding Models (CDMs) for classification, extraction, and summarization that process up to 1M tokens of multimodal text and image input in a single pass. These specialized tools are 200x faster and 467x cheaper than frontier LLM APIs, priced at $0.05 per million input tokens with no charge for output.

The models are available via ScaleDown's own API and through partners including OpenRouter, Vercel, LiteLLM, and LangChain. In accuracy tests on the CLINC OOS intent-detection benchmark, the Classify model posted a score of 95%, outperforming an average of 89.6% from three OpenAI models at 1,810x lower cost. For a limited window of 50 hours, new users receive 50M free input tokens, while OpenRouter offers a promotional rate of $0.04 per million input tokens.

selectedTweets.bestBit: 200x faster, 467x cheaper than frontier LLM APIs
selectedTweets.text:
You already gave the LLM the answer. So why is it writing it out from scratch?

Introducing a new AI model architecture: Constrained Decoding Models (CDMs)

LLMs were built to write. Most production workloads just need an answer: fast, consistent, and affordable.

CDMs are purpose-built for 1 task each. They read your input once and skip the token-by-token generative loop that makes LLMs slow and expensive.

Not just a decision model, but a family of 3 CDMs live today:

• Classify: define your labels and get back a calibrated probability + reason for each. Used for routing, tagging, and intent detection.
 • Extract: describe the entities in natural language and get back well-formed JSON with confidence scores + citations. Used for web scraping, document processing, and PII redaction.
 • Summarize: pass in long text, images, or PDFs and get back a consistent summary under 1,000 tokens. Used for context compaction, metadata generation, and transcript digests.

Built for production:

• 1M tokens of multimodal (text + image) input, 31x larger than Jev
 • 77.2% on DecisionBench vs Jev's 72%
 • 200x faster, 467x cheaper than frontier LLM APIs
 • $0.05/M input tokens. Output is free (yes, even for summarize)

selectedTweets.bestBit: The difference with regular LLMs is that these models don’t write their answer token by token
selectedTweets.text:
Pulling a due date out of a 300-page PDF shouldn’t need a model that writes.

Decision models now get a 1M-token window, and they take images too.

ScaleDown released 3 small models (Classify, Extract, Summarize) for the simple, repetitive jobs that agents usually hand to an expensive LLM.

200x faster and 467x cheaper than frontier LLM APIs. $0.05 per million input tokens, and output is free.

The bigger change is that the same design now covers classify, extract and summarize.

The difference with regular LLMs is that these models don’t write their answer token by token. They read up to 1M tokens of text and images once and pick the answer straight from the input, so output is free, results stay inside your labels or source text

ScaleDown’s Constrained Decoding Models make one prefill pass over your input and select the answer from it: a label, a span with its source offset, or the passages that belong in a summary.
